::: {.hero-banner}
MLPerf EDU turns benchmark setup, execution, quality evaluation, and provenance
into one inspectable workflow. Fourteen workloads share the same CLI and report
format. Students can begin with a functional run, then move to quality-bearing
`max` work or controlled `pro` experiments.
:::

## Start With a Guided Run

The supported preview install uses the repository and its locked environment.
The last command checks the machine, runs four small functional paths, verifies
their provenance, and writes a suite dashboard. It does not open a browser.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book
cd cs249r_book/mlperf-edu
uv sync --locked
uv run mlperf init --profile min --output-dir submissions/first-run
```

A successful first run means the local execution and artifact pipeline work.
It is not a quality score. Follow the [getting started guide](getting-started.qmd)
to read the dashboard and run the first quality-bearing benchmark.

## What a Run Produces

Every run produces HTML for people, JSON for automation, CSV for analysis, and
a `.provd.json` manifest for provenance verification. The dashboard leads with
functional readiness or the declared quality decision. It then preserves the
configuration, hardware, dataset, checkpoint lineage, and claim boundary needed
to interpret that result.

## The Suite

{{< include _stats.qmd >}}

Browse the [benchmark registry](benchmarks/index.qmd) or see the
[current readiness states](readiness.qmd). Benchmark pages are generated from
the same registry YAML that the harness reads, which keeps CLI and website
contracts aligned.

## Why It Exists

Official MLPerf suites set a high standard for benchmark governance and
measurement. They are also too operationally heavy for many classroom
settings. MLPerf EDU explores a smaller teaching and research layer while
keeping the artifacts needed for scrutiny. The [about page](about.qmd) covers
the design philosophy, independent-preview status, open licensing gates, and
proposed review path.
